sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: Render Distance controls how far terrain is rendered. Shorter distances mean less terrain is rendered, resulting in higher frame rates.
sodium.options.simulation_distance.toolt: Simulation distance controls how far terrain and entities are loaded and updated. Shorter distances reduce load on the built-in server and improve frame rates.
sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: Control the brightness (gamma) of the game.
sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scaling of the user interface. If set to "Auto", the maximum zoom factor is always used.
sodium.options.fullscreen.tooltip: If enabled, the game will appear in full screen (if supported).
sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game frame rate will be synchronized with the monitor refresh rate, this option will sacrifice input lag for a smoother gaming experience. If your configuration is too low, this setting may reduce performance.
sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limit the maximum frame rate. This helps reduce battery usage and overall system load when multitasking. This option is ignored if vertical sync is enabled and the frame rate is capped at or above the monitor's refresh rate.
sodium.options.view_bobbing.tooltip: If enabled, the player's view will shake when moving. Players who experience dizziness while playing can disable this option to alleviate symptoms.
sodium.options.attack_indicator.tooltip: Controls where the attack indicator appears on the screen.
sodium.options.autosave_indicator.toolti: If enabled, the game will display an indicator when saving a save.
sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: Default image quality controls some vanilla options and is required for mod compatibility. The options below will use this setting if they are left at Default.
sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: The quality level to follow when rendering clouds in the sky. Although this option is labeled "Fast" and "High Quality," its impact on performance is usually negligible.
sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum distance at which weather effects such as rain and snow are rendered.
sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: leaves
sodium.options.leaves_quality.tooltip: Controls whether leaves are rendered transparent (for high quality) or opaque (for fast).
sodium.options.particle_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum number of particles that can be rendered on the screen at the same time.
sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Enables smooth lighting and shading of areas within the world. This will slightly increase the time it takes to update or load chunks, but will not affect frame rate.
sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The distance at which biome colors blend smoothly into each other, in blocks. Using higher values ​​will greatly increase the time it takes to load or update chunks, and the improvement in image quality will gradually decrease.
sodium.options.entity_distance.tooltip: Distance correction multiplier for entity rendering. Smaller values ​​will reduce the maximum distance that entities can be rendered from the player, while larger values ​​will increase this distance.
sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: If enabled, a simple shadow will be rendered under creatures and other entities.
sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be applied when the player is in a darker area, making the overall image darker and more dramatic.
sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: Controls the number of mipmaps used for the block model material. Higher values ​​will improve the rendering quality of distant blocks, but may have a performance impact on resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: If enabled, only blocks within view will be rendered, which can significantly improve performance by culling large amounts of block surfaces early in the rendering process. Some resource packs may have issues using this option, so if you see blocks rendering under-rendered, try disabling this option.
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Enable fog culling
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: If enabled, blocks that are certain to be completely hidden by the fog effect will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The optimization may be more noticeable when the fog effect is heavy (such as underwater), but may result in undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some cases.
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use entity culling
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: If enabled, entities within the camera's viewport, but not within the visible block, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization leverages the visibility data that already exists for tile rendering and adds no additional overhead.
sodium.options.animate_only_visible_text: If enabled, only visible texture animations will be updated. This can significantly improve framerate on some hardware, especially with large asset packs. If you have issues with certain textures losing animation, try disabling this option.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: For debugging only. Specifies the maximum number of frames the CPU can wait for GPU rendering to complete. Changing this value is not recommended as very low or high values ​​may cause unstable framerates.
sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to:
For debugging only. If enabled, persistent memory mapping will be used for the scratch buffer to avoid unnecessary memory copies. Disabling this option may be useful to narrow down the cause of graphics corruption.

Requires OpenGL 4.4 or ARB_buffer_storage.
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Block update thread
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: Specifies the number of threads used to build chunks. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and updates, but may have a negative impact on frame times. The default value usually works in all situations.
sodium.options.always_defer_chunk_update: If enabled, entities within the camera's viewport, but not within the visible block, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization leverages the visibility data that already exists for tile rendering and adds no additional overhead.
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.name: Using a context with error checking disabled
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.tool: When enabled, an OpenGL context is created and error checking is disabled. Improves rendering performance slightly, but makes it more difficult to debug sudden, unexplained crashes.
sodium.console.game_restart: The game needs to be restarted to apply these changes!
sodium.console.broken_nvidia_driver:
Your NVIDIA driver is out of date.
  *This will create serious performance issues or cause crashes if you continue to use Sodium.
  *Please update your NVIDIA drivers to version 536.23 or newer.
sodium.console.pojav_launcher:
Sodium does not support PojavLauncher.
  *If you continue to use Sodium, you will likely experience severe performance issues, rendering errors, and crashes.
  *Please proceed at your own discretion - we will not help you solve any problems!
sodium.console.core_shaders_error: The following resource packs are incompatible with Sodium:
sodium.console.core_shaders_warn: The following resource packs may be incompatible with Sodium:
sodium.console.core_shaders_info: Please check the game log for details.
sodium.console.config_not_loaded: Sodium's configuration file is corrupted or currently unreadable. Some options have been temporarily reset to default values. Please open the Video Settings page to resolve this issue.
sodium.console.config_file_was_reset: Configuration files have been reset to known good defaults.
sodium.options.particle_quality.name: particle effects
sodium.options.use_particle_culling.name: Use particle culling
sodium.options.use_particle_culling.tool: If enabled, only visible particles will be rendered. This can significantly increase frame rate when there are many particles nearby.
sodium.options.allow_direct_memory_acces: If enabled, will allow certain critical code paths to use direct memory access to improve performance. This generally greatly reduces the CPU overhead of chunk and entity rendering, but can make diagnosing certain bugs and crashes more difficult. You should only disable it if you are asked to do so or know what you are doing.
sodium.options.enable_memory_tracing.too: Debugging capabilities. If enabled, stack traces will be collected along with memory allocations, helping to improve diagnostic information when a memory leak is detected.
sodium.options.chunk_memory_allocator.to:
Select the memory allocator used for tile rendering.
- Async: Fastest option, works with most modern graphics drivers.
- Swap: Compatibility option for older graphics drivers. May significantly increase memory usage.
modmenu.summaryTranslation.sodium: A modern rendering engine and client-side optimization mod built for Minecraft
modmenu.descriptionTranslation.sodium: Sodium is a free and open source Minecraft optimization module that can increase frame rate and reduce lag.
